statement: For general degree 2n−3 hypersurfaces in complex projective n-space, the geometric monodromy on the D_n lines is S_(D_n) for n≥4 and W(E6) for n=3. For n=2, the hypersurface is itself a single line, so D₂=1 and the monodromy is trivial.

answer.text: For general degree 2n−3 hypersurfaces in complex projective n-space, the geometric monodromy on the D_n lines is S_(D_n) for n≥4 and W(E6) for n=3. For n=2, the hypersurface is itself a single line, so D₂=1 and the monodromy is trivial.
answer.display: n≥4: S_(D_n); n=3: W(E6); n=2: trivial (D₂=1)
answer.qualification: The unrestricted complex coefficient family is used. Hashimoto–Kadets recall Harris’s monodromy computations for the cubic and higher-degree cases; the degree-one case is an elementary deduction.

source.location: Introduction, first paragraph on p. 1 (cubic surfaces) and paragraph after Theorem 1.2 on p. 2 (degree greater than three); n=2 is the elementary one-line case

scope: Generic degree 2n−3 hypersurfaces in complex projective n-space, n≥2, over the unrestricted coefficient family.
notes: The inspected source is Hashimoto–Kadets, which attributes the cubic and higher-degree line monodromy computations to Harris [Har79]. Harris’s original text was not inspected. The n=2 member is a line in P² with exactly one line on it, so its permutation action is trivial. The article’s separate alternating-or-symmetric theorem for general Fano problems is not being used in place of these exact line results.
